guard: an older cotal refuses a seed store stamped at a newer generation, and writes nothing
why: ONE MUTATION, AND IT IS THE GUARD ITSELF. Disabling the version comparison restores exactly the
behaviour this change removes: the older binary falls through, refreshes nothing, and writes its
own older generation over the stamp at the commit. So the mutation does not merely make a cell
fail, it reinstates the defect, which is the only mutation worth having here.
The anchor is CODE-ONLY and two lines wide. The single line `isStrictlyNewer(storeGeneration,
generation)` would have been unique too, but the guard's meaning lives in the pair: the validity
check is what keeps a corrupt stamp out of the comparison, and an anchor that spans both cannot
be half-disarmed by someone rewriting one of them.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, stated because the fix has a real limit. The guard ships in this
version and later. A binary RELEASED BEFORE it does not carry it and never will, so an old
cotal already on a machine can still downgrade a store it meets. That is why the smoke stamps
the store at 99.0.0 instead of running an actually-old build: 99.0.0 is newer than any binary
that will ever run the suite, which tests the comparison from the side the guard can defend.
Pointing a real v0.16.0 at a newer store reproduces the DEFECT, which is how it was found, and
